nodes.title: Adversarial review 'what she says' (safety door TS and Python, voice runtime, agents compile and simulate, calls analysis, operator): 13 reproduced defects (6 blocker, 6 major, 1 minor), each a failing test.
nodes.method: Reviewer fuzzed both doors (mixed script, Devanagari, Hinglish spellings, zero-width characters, homoglyphs, number words) and traced the voice turn loop, S2S path, identity gate and analysis. TS tests are in product/tests/review/what-she-says.test.ts (todo); Python tests in product/voice/tests/test_review.py (expectedFailure).
nodes.value: B1 plain AI denials pass; B2 any 'bot' token counts as disclosure; B3 rule split over two sentences passes; B4 'Hello? Kaun?' confirms identity; B5 per-contact amount before identity; B6 Hinglish and Tamil-English crisis lines missed; M1-M6; m1

nodes.title: The never-deny-being-an-AI rule was a block list of denial shapes (RD2 claims_human); short natural denials matched none of them.
nodes.broke: 'Ji nahi, main bot nahi.', 'मैं machine नहीं, Riya हूँ।' and 'बिल्कुल इंसान हूँ।' reached TTS unchanged. The voice runtime also counted any 'bot' token as the disclosure. Rule: self-reference about her own nature is allowed only when it affirms AI-ness (an allow-list that over-triggers). A false positive costs one honest sentence; a false negative breaks a non-negotiable.

events.details: safety: B1 (allow-list self-reference rule), B5, B6, M1, m1, M2 (normalisation as a shared contract in rules.json). voice: B2, B3 (judge with the previous sentence), B4 (identity only on explicit affirmation, fail closed), B5 port, M3 (S2S audio gated on the door or the stack is barred from production), M4, M5. agents: B3 in simulate.ts. calls: M6 (outcome evidence must be a caller turn).
